draft.title: Sampling methods
card: A population is the whole group we want to know about. A sample is a smaller part of it that we collect data from.
Random
every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen, such as drawing names from a hat.
Systematic
choose every kth member from a list, after a random start. For 500 students and a sample of 50, take every 10th name.
Stratified

split the population into groups, such as year groups, then take a random sample from each group in proportion to its size. A self-selected sample is different: people choose themselves, such as in an online poll. Mostly people with strong views reply, so it can be biased.
draft.remember: A fair sample gives every member a chance of being chosen. A sample that people choose for themselves can be biased.

a.q: A school has 500 students on a numbered list. The principal picks a random start, then surveys every 10th student on the list. Which sampling method is this?
opts: Systematic
Stratified
Self-selected
Simple random
a.why: Choosing every kth name from a list after a random start is systematic sampling. It is not stratified, because the students are not split into groups first.
a.clue: Look at how the students are picked from the list.

b.q: A council in Wagga Wagga wants to know if residents like a new bus timetable. It posts a survey link on its Facebook page and uses the first 200 replies. Why might the results be biased?
opts: Residents chose themselves, so replies may differ from the town
The sample of 200 is too small to be called a sample
Every resident had an equal chance of being chosen
The residents were split into groups before being chosen
b.why: This is a self-selected sample. Only residents who see the page and want to reply take part, so their views may differ from the whole town. The size of 200 is not the problem.
b.clue: Who decided which residents took part?

problems.detail: The self-selected sample is described inside the Stratified bullet. A student could read self-selection as part of stratified sampling. It needs its own bullet.

'A fair sample gives every member a chance of being chosen' drops the word 'equal' that the card uses. An online poll also gives every member a chance to reply, so this line does not separate fair samples from self-selected ones. It should say 'an equal chance'.

The right option is the longest and the only one with a qualifier ('may'). It is also the only option that gives a reason for bias. The other three describe things that would not cause bias, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: Sampling methods
card: Random
every member of the population, the whole group being studied, has an equal chance of being in the sample, such as drawing names from a hat.
Systematic
choose every kth member from a list, after a random start. For 500 students and a sample of 50, take every 10th name.
Stratified
split the population into groups, such as year groups, then take a random sample from each group in proportion to its size.
Self-selected
people choose to take part, such as in an online poll. People with strong views are more likely to reply, so the sample can be biased: its results may not match the population.
proposal.remember: A fair sample gives every member an equal chance of being chosen. A sample whose members choose themselves can be biased.
